abstract: We study the existence of standing wave solutions for the following quasilinear Schrödinger equations with critical growth on the Heisenberg group $$ -Δ_{\mathbb{H}} u +V(ξ)u-Δ_{\mathbb{H}} (\left|u\right|^{2α})\left|u\right|^{2α-2} u= λ\left|u\right|^{q-2}u + \left|u\right|^{p-2}u \text{ in }\mathbb{H}^N $$ where $\mathbb{H}^N$ is Heisenberg group, $Δ_{\mathbb{H}}$ is Kohn Laplacian operator, $4α \frac{1}{2}.$ By a suitable nonlinear change of variables, the quasilinear equation is transformed into a semilinear one, allowing the use of variational methods in the Folland--Stein Sobolev space $S^{1,2}(\mathbb{H}^N)$. Applying the mountain pass theorem together with a concentration--compactness argument adapted to the sub-Riemannian framework, we establish the existence of a nontrivial solution.
title: Quasilinear Schrödinger Critical Problem on the Heisenberg group \(\mathbb{H}^N\)
